chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from the son of his brother al-Fudayl ibn Yasar said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a woman entered, and I was the closest of the people to her. She said to me, 'Ask him for me.' I said, 'About what?' She said, 'My son died and left wealth that was in the hand of my brother, and he squandered it. Then he acquired more wealth and deposited it with me. Should I take from it for myself an amount equal to what he squandered?' So I informed him of that, and he said, 'No.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Return the trust to the one who entrusted you, and do not betray the one who betrayed you.'
ai.seo_question: Can a trustee deduct losses caused by the depositor's squandering from the deposited wealth according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the principle of *amanah* (trustworthiness) by ruling that a trustee must return the deposited wealth in full, regardless of the depositor's prior squandering of other assets. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly distinction between the specific obligation of returning a trust and the general right of compensation, emphasizing that fidelity to the trust is not contingent on the trustee's reciprocal fairness. The Prophet’s maxim cited here serves as a foundational ethical guideline for maintaining integrity in financial dealings even amidst personal grievance.
